summary: Perf-canary job flakiness on L40S CI runners (intermittent GPU dropouts / Xid errors) causing false regressions for hardware profile pack
environment: CI (perf-canary), runner pool: gpu-l40s-ci, region: us-east
content:
Issue Summary
- Perf-canary runs on L40S runners have become intermittently flaky (runner-level failures) since enabling the expanded workload matrix runner (benchmark-lab PR-1842) and adding profile-specific gates (perf-canary PR-731).
- Failures present as GPU disappearing mid-run or driver/library mismatch on a subset of nodes. This is causing false perf regressions and blocking merges related to the hardware tuning profiles pack.

Impact
- Internal: ~18–30% of L40S perf-canary builds fail on first attempt, typically within 10–25 minutes.
- External: No direct customer impact; however, this is delaying rollout readiness for L40S profile changes and increasing risk of shipping without stable regression detection.

Observed Failure Modes (examples)
1) GPU drop / Xid error during decode phase
- In CI logs:
  - "CUDA error: unspecified launch failure"
  - "RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered"
  - "nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0) failed: Unknown Error"
- Node dmesg (captured from failed runner):
  - "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:17:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus"
  - "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:17:00): 43, ChID 0007, pid=..., Graphics SM Warp Exception"

2) Driver/library mismatch on subset of L40S nodes (deterministic per node)
- In CI logs:
  - "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"
  - "nvmlInit_v2() failed"

3) Host-level pressure leading to timeouts (less frequent)
- In CI logs:
  - "perf-runner: heartbeat missed (120s)"
  - "context deadline exceeded waiting for metrics artifact upload"

Scope / Where it happens
- Only L40S runner pool (gpu-l40s-ci) is affected.
- H100 CI runners do not show elevated flake rate.
- Repro is not tied to a specific model; happens across the workload matrix, more commonly on long-context buckets.

Hypotheses (initial)
- Infra variance in L40S runner pool:
  - Mixed NVIDIA driver versions after partial AMI rollout.
  - A small number of nodes showing recurrent Xid errors (likely hardware instability, PCIe issues, or thermal/power events).
- Secondary: artifact upload timeouts due to noisy neighbor on CI egress, but this does not explain NVML mismatch.

Triage Data
- Affected nodes (from perf-canary runner labels + logs): l40s-ci-12, l40s-ci-19, l40s-ci-22 (highest failure frequency).
- Driver versions observed:
  - Good nodes: 550.90.07
  - Bad nodes: 545.29.06 (and one node with 550 user-space libs but 545 kernel module per NVML mismatch)

Immediate Mitigation
- Re-run strategy: perf-canary currently retries once; not sufficient when the runner is pinned to the same unhealthy node.
- Node quarantine: drain/remove nodes with recurrent Xid events from the L40S CI pool.

Resolution (as of 2025-12-15)
- Drained 3 unhealthy nodes with repeated Xid 79/43 events and replaced them.
- Completed AMI/driver reconciliation for gpu-l40s-ci pool to ensure a single driver baseline (550.90.07) and consistent user-space libraries.
- Added a preflight check in the runner startup script:
  - Validate driver/library match (nvmlInit)
  - Validate nvidia-smi health and persistence mode enabled
  - Fail-fast the node and mark it unschedulable for CI if checks fail
- Updated perf-canary scheduler to avoid sticky assignment to a single runner on retry (retry must land on a different node).

Follow-ups / Action Items
- (Infra) Add automated node health scoring for CI GPU pools using Xid counters + nvml health; auto-drain on threshold.
- (Perf-canary) Add a clear failure classification so Xid/driver mismatch failures are flagged as INFRA_FLAKE and do not page Runtime.
- (Benchmarking) Reduce long-context bucket concurrency on L40S runners until we have 2 weeks of clean signal; confirm no change to measured perf deltas.

References
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread "l40s ooms under long context matrix run" (1763615572)
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread "perf-canary thresholds too noisy" (1764307714)
- Confluence: Perf-canary gates for hardware profiles

Customer-facing notes
- None. Internal CI stability incident only.

We’re seeing L40S perf-canary failures that don’t reproduce locally and disappear on rerun. Top signatures: "GPU has fallen off the bus" and NVML mismatch. This is blocking merges for profile pack work. Attaching snippets:
- "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"
- dmesg: "NVRM: Xid ... 79, GPU has fallen off the bus"
Can Infra confirm whether the gpu-l40s-ci pool is fully updated to the new driver/AMI?

2025-12-11 10:02 PT — Aisha Bello
Confirm elevated flake rate on L40S canary jobs since the workload-matrix runner started running long-context buckets. H100 gates are stable. Failures do not line up with perf regressions (no consistent metric deltas prior to crash). Suggest classifying as INFRA_FLAKE and rerouting retry to a different node.

2025-12-11 11:37 PT — Vanessa Ortiz (Assignee)
Infra check: gpu-l40s-ci pool is in mixed state. Found ~20% nodes still on older driver (545.29.06). One node has 550 user-space libs + 545 kernel module (likely from partial update / cached container layer). Plan:
1) Drain l40s-ci-12/l40s-ci-19/l40s-ci-22 immediately.
2) Roll forward remaining nodes to 550.90.07 and invalidate cached NVIDIA libs in base image.
Will post updates + list of drained instance IDs in #eng-infra.

2025-12-12 08:20 PT — Keiko Yamamoto
Adding note: L40S nodes are PCIe; we’ve previously seen Xid 79 correlate with flaky PCIe link / power events. Draining is the right short-term move. Longer-term we should set up Xid-based auto-quarantine for CI pools similar to what we do for prod dedicated pools.

2025-12-12 15:11 PT — Vanessa Ortiz
Update: Drained the 3 worst offenders; re-imaged 7 remaining nodes to unify driver baseline (550.90.07). NVML mismatch no longer reproduces on new nodes. Remaining flake is only the occasional artifact upload timeout (separate issue; likely CI egress).

2025-12-13 10:46 PT — Kira Volkov
Requested: can we add a runner preflight that fails fast if nvmlInit fails OR if dmesg contains recent Xid entries? Even a simple grep on boot would prevent wasting 20 minutes of perf run before failing. Also request: retry must land on a different node (avoid sticky retry).

2025-12-14 09:05 PT — Vanessa Ortiz
Implemented preflight in runner bootstrap:
- nvidia-smi -L
- python nvml init check
- enable persistence mode
- collect and publish nvidia-smi -q summary as artifact for failed runs
Also changed the CI scheduler to anti-affinity on retry (different node). Pushed config at 08:40 PT.

2025-12-15 16:22 PT — Sahana Iyer
Validated over weekend: 42 L40S perf-canary runs, 0 NVML mismatch failures, 0 Xid-related dropouts. Marking resolved. Remaining occasional artifact-upload timeout is low-frequency and tracked separately. Thanks all.
